jcr:content.jcr:title: Retroactive Leave of Absence Undergraduate And Second Bachelor's Degree Students

text.text:
ATTN: For GRADUATE AND CREDENTIAL STUDENT retroactive leave of absence, please go to:

https://www.fullerton.edu/graduate/current/forms.html(click on the link for the 'Retroactive Leave of Absence')

What does Stop-Out policy have to do with my request for a leave of absence?
Undergraduate and post-baccalaureate second bachelor's students who need to be absent from the University should first make use of a stop-out semester before seeking to use the leave of absence policy, as explained below.

IMPORTANT - ARE ALL STUDENTS ELIGIBLE FOR USING THE STOP-OUT POLICY? No
Not eligible for a stop-out semester:

  • Academically disqualified students
  • Foreign visa students
  • Graduate students
  • Credential students

Students who have been on an approved leave of absence for two semesters or more cannot add a stop-out semester at the end of their approved leave period in an effort to extend their period of absence from the university.

Stop-Out Policy

  • Pertains to Spring and Fall semesters only (Summer Session & Intersession do not count as terms that are a part of the stop-out policy)
  • No form to fill out (can be non-enrolled for one semester)
  • Must return to enrolled status in the semester immediately following a stop-out semester
  • Registration information will be automatically available for the term following stop-out
  • Can be used more than once, but not for two semesters in a row (students are not permitted to use stop-out policy for consecutive semesters)
  • Cannot be used the first semester you are admitted to CSUF

Example: (please note: Intersession and Summer Session do not pertain to stop-out policy)

Spring 2015 Fall 2015 Spring 2016 Fall 2016 Spring 2017 Fall 2017 Spring 2018
Enrolled On STOP-OUT MUST enroll(or request Leave of Absence) Enrolled Enrolled On STOP-OUT MUST enroll(or request Leave of Absence)

 

WARNING: If the student does not enroll in the semester immediately following a stop-out semester, the student is discontinued and must apply for readmission to Cal State Fullerton should the student wish to return as a matriculated student.

Retroactive Leave of Absence Policy: If the student has used a stop-out semester (stop-out does not apply to graduate or credential students), but still needs to be absent from the university, the student can submit a request for a leave of absence if the reason for the request is one of the circumstances listed on the leave of absence request form that follows these instructions. Leave of Absence requests should be submitted prior to the start of the term for which a leave of absence is requested. However, a retroactive leave of absence may be considered only for serious medical issues or other extenuating circumstances that prevented timely registration or submitting a leave of absence request prior to the start of the term. The retroactive leave of absence will be reviewed by all appropriate departments and can either be granted or denied. When submitting a retroactive leave of absence request:

  • Make sure you first make use of a stop-out semester (if eligible to use stop-out, as explained above)
  • Make sure the reason for your retroactive leave request is one of the reasons listed on the form
  • Complete and sign the 'Request for Retroactive Leave of Absence' form
  • Attach documentation as explained below

Documentation for a Retroactive Leave of Absence It is important to provide appropriate and thorough documentation for your retroactive leave of absence. If your Retroactive Leave of Absence request is submitted without any documentation, your form will be returned to you without processing. The form can only be resubmitted when appropriate documentation is attached.

  • An attached statement from the student describing the reason for requesting a retroactive leave of absence is not considered documentation.
  • Documentation must be from a source other than the student to verify the reason for the request and the reason a request for a leave of absence wasn’t submitted prior to the start of the term (example: letter from a health care provider, military orders, study abroad contract, etc).
